claims.text: He is one man with two names in the corpus. The Internet Archive's catalogue records give the authorised form of his name on every work as 'Menzel, Donald H. (Donald Howard), 1901-1976', which resolves the batch 05 caption 'Howard Menzel' to the batch 02 'Donald Menzel'.
His last debunking book appeared a year after his death: 'The UFO enigma: the definitive explanation of the UFO phenomenon', Garden City, N.Y.: Doubleday, 1977, ISBN 0385035969.

label: Donald H. Menzel
narrative: Donald Howard Menzel, 1901-1976, was the director of the Harvard College Observatory and the period's most prominent scientific opponent of the extraterrestrial hypothesis. The board's interest is not his astronomy but the fact that the Air Force's own commissioned study endorsed him: in the Condon Report's history chapter, written by Condon himself, Menzel's 1953 Flying Saucers is called 'an excellent book' and is noted as 'generally regarded as "debunking" and "negative."' That is a study accused of reaching a predetermined conclusion praising, in its own text, the man whose conclusion it reached. The claim the Area 52 corpus attaches to him, that Stanton Friedman found in his Harvard papers in April 1986 a thirty-year NSA association and a CIA Top Secret Ultra clearance, could not be opened from here and is carried as a gap, not as a fact.
